content.text:
Your clone has uncommitted changes, and `main` is one commit ahead of `origin/main`. Stash your working files before merging; your existing commit will be preserved.

The URL you supplied appears to contain a typo (`github.com.GitRollTraining`). Assuming you meant `github.com/GitRollTraining`, run:

```bash
# Save uncommitted changes, including untracked files
git stash push -u -m "Local changes before upstream merge"

# Add the original repository as upstream
git remote add upstream https://github.com/GitRollTraining/ai-full-stack-it-access-requests.git

# Fetch and merge upstream changes into main
git fetch upstream
git switch main
git merge upstream/main

# Restore your uncommitted changes
git stash pop

# Review the result
git status
```

If the merge reports conflicts, edit the conflicting files, then run:

```bash
git add <resolved-file>
git merge --continue
```

Then resume with `git stash pop`. Conflicts during stash restoration also require editing and staging the affected files; Git retains the stash if restoration encounters conflicts.

Once you’ve reviewed and tested the result, update your fork:

```bash
git push origin main
```

No force push is needed.

```text
origin  https://github.com/shantha012/ai-full-stack-it-access-requests.git (fetch)
origin  https://github.com/shantha012/ai-full-stack-it-access-requests.git (push)
```

Only your fork is configured. No `upstream` remote has been added yet.
